lesson.menu_desc: Reading the subtext of vague messages from Penang, Monterrey and the CFO -- and replying with so / not (I suppose so, I'm afraid not)
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 27 -- Navigating Ambiguity -- Substitution with so and not in short replies (I think so, I'm afraid not)

lesson.grammar_point: substitution with so and not in short replies (I think so, I'm afraid not)

listenings.text: Hi Fabiana, it's Lucia. Thank you for the email about the extra volume for October. So, in principle, it should be fine. My team is very motivated, and we really want to help after everything that happened in Penang. There are just a few small things we need to check. Two of our four lines have a maintenance window in October, which was planned months ago. And for extra shifts, I would need to talk to the union first, and that can take a little time. I'm sure we can find a way. Maybe, if it's possible, we could talk about November instead? Or part in October and part in November? Let me know what you think. A quick call would probably be easier than email.

Hey Fabiana, it's Daniel. I was in the budget meeting this morning, and I know you're waiting for news, so here's what I heard. The CFO called your proposal interesting, and he said it was worth looking at in the next budget cycle. Now, I've worked with him for six years, so let me translate. Interesting is not exciting. And the next budget cycle means not now. He also didn't ask a single question, which usually means he isn't going to fight for it. So my reading is lukewarm, not dead. My advice: don't read too much into one meeting. Ask Priya for fifteen minutes with him before the budget closes, and bring one number, the cost of those twelve days in July. Numbers change his mind. Adjectives don't.

extra_audio.text: Fabiana explains to Priya how she read the three messages. First, Hafiz wrote that his team would do their best to meet the November date. Marcus told her not to take that at face value, because in Penang it's often a polite no. Then Lucia sent mixed signals: in principle it was fine, but two lines are in maintenance. After that, the CFO's office sent a lukewarm email about revisiting the numbers in due course. So, will they get the budget this month? I'm afraid not, but a revised version is still possible.

items.situation: Priya asks: Will Penang really make the November date?
tips: I don't think so. Hafiz said they'd do their best, and that's usually a polite no.
I don't think so + one reason.

items.situation: Marcus asks: Is the resilience budget approved?
tips: I'm afraid not. The CFO's office wants a revised version in due course.
I'm afraid not: bad news, politely.

items.situation: Lucia asks: Could we move part of the volume to November?
tips: I suppose so, as long as we confirm the October part in writing.
I suppose so: a reluctant yes.

items.situation: Daniel asks: Will the CFO give you fifteen minutes?
tips: I hope so. Priya is asking him this week.
I hope so: you want it, but you're not sure.

items.situation: A colleague says the CFO's email means the project is dead.
tips: I don't think so. It's lukewarm, but it isn't a no. Let's not read too much into one email.
read into + I don't think so.
